In South Korea, call 112 for police, 119 for ambulance/medical emergency, and 119 for fire services.

South Korea has a Universal (National Health Insurance / 국민건강보험 — mandatory for residents) healthcare system, rated excellent quality. Typical costs for tourists: System: Universal (National Health Insurance / 국민건강보험 — mandatory for residents) Quality: ★★★★★ (5/5) Excellent healthcare system with world-class hospitals and advanced technology. English is available at larger hospitals in Seoul and Busan but limited elsewhere. Healthcare is affordable by Western standards. National Health Insurance does NOT cover tourists — you pay out-of-pocket or through travel insurance. 💡 Medical Tourism South Korea is a major medical tourism destination, particularly for cosmetic surgery, dermatology, and advanced medical treatments. High quality at moderate costs.. Pharmacy access: easy. Access: easy Hours: Most pharmacies (약국) open 9am-9pm. Some are open 24/7 in larger cities. Look for the green '약' sign. Some medications are available only at hospitals, not regular pharmacies. Prescription rules: Most medications require a Korean doctor's prescription. Foreign prescriptions are NOT accepted. You must see a Korean doctor to get a prescription. Some controlled substances require special permits. 💡 Tips Pharmacies are widely available. Many medications require a prescription. Some common medications are available OTC. Prescription medications must be dispensed at a pharmacy with a valid Korean prescription. Hospital prescriptions can be filled at external pharmacies. Recommended vaccinations: Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, COVID-19 (following current guidelines), MMR (ensure routine vaccines are current). Malaria risk is negligible. Travel insurance advice: ⚠️ Strongly recommended Average cost: $35-60/week 💡 Tip National Health Insurance does not cover tourists. Large hospitals often require payment upfront or guarantee of payment from your insurance. International clinics are popular with tourists. Andong Hahoe is a destination in South Korea. Andong Hahoe earns its keep with deep history, strong sense of place, and the kind of cultural density that anchors an itinerary easily. Known for: Cultural, Romantic, History. Budget level: $$. Best time to visit: Oct–May. Currency: South Korean won (KRW). Primary language: Korean. Tap water is safe to drink. Tipping: Tipping is generally not expected outside some luxury contexts.. Visa: Visa rules depend on your passport and trip length; verify requirements before booking..

Andong is a destination in South Korea. A heritage-heavy Korea stop that pays off for travelers who want tradition without Seoul-scale noise. Known for: Cultural, Relaxation, Unfrequented. Budget level: $$. Best time to visit: Apr–May, Sep–Oct. Currency: South Korean won (KRW). Primary language: Korean. Tap water is safe to drink.
